abstraction_design.rationale: The VM-seam design (server builds compact models, pages render them) is built around the app's real variation and stretches to similar resources with high reuse; the misses are the under-powered `CardList`, the duplicated TTL cache, and minor boolean-flag creep.

findings.issue: The card-grid markup is duplicated three times (CardList, home.html, team-page.html) because CardList cannot pass types or per-item extras to PokemonCard; the team feature copied the grid instead of extending the abstraction.
findings.suggestion: Give CardList a `types` passthrough and an `<ng-content>` slot for per-item actions (Remove buttons, priority), then use it from home and team so a card-list change lands in one template.

findings.issue: The TTL/promise cache is implemented twice — server (api-client.ts, bounded at 4000 entries) and client (app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:21, unbounded) — with slightly different rules.
findings.suggestion: Extract one `ttlCache(ttlMs, maxEntries)` helper (shared/ is the natural home) and use it in both places so caching rules change once.

findings.issue: TeamVM.coverage is computed server-side and shipped in every /_data and TransferState payload, but the team page ignores it and recomputes from `vm.attackTypes` (app/src/app/pages/team/team-page.ts:29); the field is dead weight and a 'which is the source of truth?' trap.
findings.suggestion: Drop `coverage` from TeamVM (keep `attackTypes`), or render `vm.coverage` initially and only recompute after client-side edits.

findings.issue: The sprite URL scheme (`/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png`) is constructed inside a UI component, which also injects API_BASE_URL and duplicates the default base already in api-client.ts (app/src/server/api-client.ts:12 vs app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:42).
findings.suggestion: Move sprite-URL construction into the data layer (add `sprite` to the Card/VM) so a media-URL or data-source change doesn't touch a presentational component.

findings.issue: Routes map to page-data paths by hand (`/types/:name` → `/type/<name>`, singular) so the URL scheme and the path protocol must be kept in sync manually; adding a page means remembering the singular/plural convention.
findings.suggestion: Derive the page-data path from the route pattern (or use the real URL as the key) so the mapping is uniform and grep-friendly.

findings.issue: The title strategy depends on the magic resolver key `'vm'` and duck-types `{title?}` on every page's data, so a page that resolves under a different key silently gets a wrong title.
findings.suggestion: Type the contract once (e.g., `interface TitledData { title?: string | null }` used by the resolvers) or key titles off route data set by the resolver.

findings.issue: `typeRef` label-fallback logic is duplicated between the home component and the server loader (loaders.ts:118), so a label rule change needs two edits.
findings.suggestion: Export the `typeRef(name, labels)` helper from shared/ and reuse it in home.ts.

findings.issue: Minor inconsistency: `@Injectable()` here while the rest of the codebase uses the current `@Service()` decorator (team-store.ts:12, page-data.ts:44).
findings.suggestion: Use `@Service({autoProvided: false})` (it is provided via `useClass`) for consistency with the project's convention.

summary: A coherent, idiomatic Angular 22 codebase: dumb components over narrow view models, an explicit PAGE_DATA_LOADER seam between server loaders and the browser, pure shared logic reused on both sides, and no experimental APIs. Most changes land in one obvious place; the recurring editability tax is that per-page wiring is spread across routes, the loaders.ts switch, and models.ts, and that CardList, the TTL cache, and the card-grid markup are each duplicated two or three times. The team feature fits the existing architecture well, though it left one dead VM field and copied the grid rather than extending the shared component.

The catch: the card only receives `id` and species `name`, so if the fix needs the default Pokémon's name/document you must thread it through Card + toCards + loadHome + loadTeam first.

All findable, but a caching-rule change must be made twice.
